precepts.text: The open face: Daniel set his face unto the Lord God, to seek by prayer and supplications, with fasting, and sackcloth, and ashes. He understood by books, by the writings of Jeremiah the prophet, the number of the years. He went to the book, then made his confession: we have sinned, and have committed iniquity, and have done wickedly, by departing from thy precepts. Neither have we hearkened unto thy servants the prophets: they would not listen to the servants God sent to show them what they were doing wrong.
precepts.point: But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory. When we behold the glass openly, we change. There is supposed to be a change in us.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
“But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord”. This book is the glass of the glory of the Lord, and we behold it with an open face. What is the open face? Daniel shows it: “And I set my face unto the Lord God, to seek by prayer and supplications, with fasting, and sackcloth, and ashes”. He went to God openly by prayer and supplication.

But first, “I Daniel understood by books the number of the years, whereof the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, that he would accomplish seventy years in the desolations of Jerusalem.” Seeking God openly, he went to the book, the writings of Jeremiah. Then he made his confession: “We have sinned, and have committed iniquity, and have done wickedly, and have rebelled, even by departing from thy precepts and from thy judgments”.

“Neither have we hearkened unto thy servants the prophets, which spake in thy name to our kings, our princes, and our fathers, and to all the people of the land.” They would not listen to the servants God sent to show them what they were doing wrong.

So when we really behold his face openly, we “are changed into the same image from glory to glory”. There is supposed to be a change in us when we pray, accept and understand that we have sinned against God. We behold ourselves in these books, and what we see there is there for us to fix. The worst thing to do is deny it, or refuse to hearken to the prophets he sends to show us how to get right.

precepts.text: Seeing we have this ministry, we faint not; but have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty. When you seek his face openly, you renounce the secret sins: not walking in craftiness, not talking your way around it, nor handling the word of God deceitfully, but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man's conscience. Blessed is the man whose conscience does not condemn him, because he examined himself against the word and renounced what he was doing. But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost: if you do not understand that you have to renounce sin, you are lost. That is the Christian church: we are not under the law, we are under grace, you cannot call me a sinner, I am saved; yet the hidden things have never been renounced. Your religion is vain if the secret life never changes.
precepts.point: But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory. When we behold the glass openly, we change. There is supposed to be a change in us.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
Beholding with open face, we are changed. Then chapter 4: “Therefore seeing we have this ministry, as we have received mercy, we faint not; But have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty”. That is what we are supposed to do when we seek him openly, face to face: renounce the hidden things, the secret sins.

“not walking in craftiness”: not talking too much, trying to find a way to snake around it, “nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.” Blessed is the man whose conscience does not condemn him, because he has examined himself against this book, renounced what he was doing, and no longer does it.

“But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost”. If you do not understand that you have to behold with an open face and renounce sin, you are lost. That is the Christian church: we are no longer under the laws of God, we are under grace, you can't call me a sinner, I've been saved. Bro, what are you talking about? You have not renounced the hidden things of dishonesty. You're an undercover homo. You're still fornicating, still smoking weed, effeminate, popping gum with your sister's lip gloss on. You have not renounced it, so you are lost.

If you think you found God while the secret life never changes, your religion is vain. It is a level of insanity to ask God to deal with you and then not do what God says. The change from glory to glory comes only when the hidden things are renounced.

precepts.text: Surely he knoweth your inventions, and what ye think in your hearts, even them that sin, and would hide their sins. You cannot openly seek his face while you are hiding your sins.
precepts.point: But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory. When we behold the glass openly, we change. There is supposed to be a change in us.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
Paul says we “have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty”. Why must they be renounced and not hidden? “Surely he knoweth your inventions, and what ye think in your hearts, even them that sin, and would hide their sin.”

God knows your inventions and the thoughts of your heart. He knows them that sin and would hide their sin. You cannot openly seek his face while you are hiding your sins, trying to get around them and not deal with them.

The open face of 2 Corinthians 3:18 is a face with nothing hidden. Beholding the glory of the Lord in his book means seeing what is there about ourselves and bringing it into the light: not walking in craftiness, not snaking around it, not handling the word of God deceitfully.

So the man who hides his sin is not beholding with an open face, and he is not changed into the same image from glory to glory. He only fools himself, because the Lord already knows what he thinks in his heart.

precepts.text: I brought you up with gladness, but with sorrow and heaviness have I lost you: for ye have sinned before the Lord your God. The gospel is hid to them that are lost, to him that is still in sin and will not renounce the hidden things of dishonesty.
precepts.point: But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory. When we behold the glass openly, we change. There is supposed to be a change in us.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
“But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost”. Who are the lost? Ezra shows it: “I brought you up with gladness; but with sorrow and heaviness have I lost you: for ye have sinned before the Lord your God, and done that thing that is evil before him.”

The gospel is hid to them that are lost: to him that is still in sin and has not renounced the hidden things of dishonesty. Those are the ones that are lost, still in sin, refusing to stop being dishonest and living as a sinner. If you think you found God while you live like that, you are lost. Your religion is vain and you do not really believe.

“But what shall I now do unto you? I am a widow and forsaken: go your way, O my children, and ask mercy of the Lord.”

So beholding the glory of the Lord with an open face must bring a change. Christ showed Peter his errors before he was converted, telling him he would deny him thrice, and afterward Peter was the head of the church. God opens his book and shows us, and sends prophets to show us how to get right. It does not feel good, like medicine, but if you are sincere you take it and get better. If you do not, you remain lost, and you become an example of what not to do.

precepts.text: Through this man is preached the forgiveness of sins, and by him all that believe are justified from all things from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses: all things, not almost all.
precepts.point: The veil on Moses' face symbolised Christ and Israel's blindness to the end of that which is abolished; the same veil is on the Pharisees in the reading of the Old Testament, blinded by their covetousness so they had him killed, and it is done away in Christ when they turn to the Lord. Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty: atonement for all the things you could not atone under Moses.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
Paul says we are “able ministers of the new testament; not of the letter, but of the spirit: for the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life.” The letter is the old testament, the Mosaic law of sacrifice. The spirit is Christ's death. The letter kills: if you despised Moses' law, you died without mercy. We read earlier that almost all things are purged with blood. Almost all things you could atone for, if there was an animal for it. But if there was no animal for it, whose blood got shed? Yours. That is condemnation, and condemnation and death are the same.

How does the spirit give life? “Be it known unto you therefore, men and brethren, that through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins”. That is life. “And by him all that believe are justified from all things”. Not almost all things: all things. Everything you can think of, Christ died for, which the animals could not do. You can repent under Christ's death; under animals, you cannot.

“from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses”: that law is the sacrifice, the law of sin and death, the ministration of condemnation. That is why Paul said in Galatians that if you want to go by that sacrifice, you are a debtor to do the whole law, including sacrificing animals, and the temple is destroyed, so you had better figure it out.

So the ministration of death, “written and engraven in stones”, was glorious, but “much more doth the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory”, because under Christ you can atone for everything you could not atone for under Moses. “where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty”: freedom from the law of sin and death.

precepts.text: Their minds were blinded; the same vail remaineth in the reading of the old testament, done away in Christ; when it shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away.
precepts.point: Leaders of other camps do not show up at IUIC schools unannounced and then complain on video about not being let in. There are channels; call first. The camps do not fellowship because of doctrine, and one GMS member sat in a school for months living a double life.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
“And not as Moses, which put a vail over his face, that the children of Israel could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished”. Moses spent time with the Lord, and the Lord's glory was upon him so that he was blinding; he had to wear a vail. The shine on Moses represented the new covenant: the glory of Christ was on Moses, and the people could not look at Moses just as they could not see Christ in the Old Testament.

“But their minds were blinded”. Not their eyes; their minds. How is your mind blinded? You read the Bible and say, I don't see it, when it is right there. Nations can't be saved: I don't see it. Israelite: I don't see it. Then, “for until this day remaineth the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament; which vail is done away in Christ.” When it comes to reading the Old Testament, they are still blinded as they were with Moses, blinded to Christ and to the northern kingdom being brought back in.

“But even unto this day, when Moses is read, the vail is upon their heart”: they don't understand the prophets. “Nevertheless when it shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away”: when they repent, they will see Christ. “Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty”, liberty from keeping animal sacrifice.

That is the mist of darkness Peter speaks of, and the only way out of it is turning to the Lord. Keep God's commandments and laws; it works for us.

precepts.point: So the clay was moulded and set down, and the question the rest of the class answers is who the breath of life was.
